### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd edition), Example 10.4, §10.2, printed page 270 (PDF page 279) — item `awodey:10.2:example4`.

Awodey states the same obligation in the poset form: a monad on a poset is a monotone map that is inflationary (`x ≤ Tx`) and satisfies `T²x ≤ Tx`, and the two inequalities force `T² = T`, so `T` is a closure operation (topological closure and the modal possibility operator are his instances). This is the thin-category case of the theorem already scoped here, and the derivation of idempotency **from** thinness is the part with no in-tree counterpart today: the only monad-level idempotency notion in the tree is `Construction/Reflective/Idempotent.v:81`'s `IdempotentMonad`, which takes join-invertibility as a hypothesis and derives nothing from thinness.

No extra checkbox: the existing scope ("monads on a preorder **are** closure operators") already covers the derivation in both directions.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd edition), §10.2, unnumbered construction, printed page 271 (PDF page 280) — item `awodey:10.2:construction-poset-monad-adjunction`.

Awodey follows the closure-operator example with the recovery of an adjunction from it: let `K = im(T)` be the sub-poset of fixed points with inclusion `i : K → P` monic and `t : P → K` the factorisation of `T` (so `T = i ∘ t`); from `TTp = Tp` one gets `t i k = k`, and then `p ≤ i k` iff `t p ≤ k`, i.e. `t ⊣ i`, an adjunction of posets whose induced monad is `T`. It is the concrete, order-theoretic instance of "every monad arises from an adjunction".

In-tree state: the general form exists one level up but with different hypotheses — `Construction/Reflective/Idempotent.v:335` `idem_reflective_adj : idem_reflector ⊣ Incl C MLocal_Subcategory` (the fixed-point subcategory is reflective), `:345` `Idempotent_Reflective`, `:464` `Idempotent_EM_Equivalence`. Two things are missing there: it must be *handed* an `IdempotentMonad` rather than getting idempotency from thinness, and nothing states that the monad induced by that reflective adjunction is the original one (only the converse direction, `Reflective_Monad` at `:194-198`, is proved).

- [ ] (from Awodey §10.2) the fixed-point factorisation `T = i ∘ t` with `t ⊣ i` for the inclusion of the sub-poset of closed elements, **and** the identification of the monad induced by that adjunction with the original `T`.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd edition), Example 10.5, §10.2, printed page 271 (PDF page 280) — item `awodey:10.2:example5`.

Same monad, same components: the covariant powerset functor with `P(f) = im(f)`, unit the singleton map `x ↦ {x}`, multiplication the union `α ↦ ⋃α`. Awodey offers it as an example of a monad with no evident underlying adjunction and leaves naturality and the monad laws to the reader.

In-tree state confirming the gap is real: no covariant powerset endofunctor exists anywhere (`Structure/Topos.v:129`'s `Pow a := Ω ^ a` is an internal power object; `Instance/Rel.v` uses `Ensemble` only as a hom type; `Instance/Ens.v` is a category whose *objects* are ensembles), and none of the tree's categorical monad instances is a powerset monad.

No extra checkbox: Awodey's version is contained in the existing scope.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd edition), Exercise 10.6.5, printed page 291 (PDF page 300) — item `awodey:10:ex5`.

The exercise is the verification half of the example above: show that the covariant powerset functor with the singleton unit and the union multiplication is a monad on sets, i.e. check naturality of both transformations and the unit and associativity laws. It adds no obligation beyond this issue's existing scope; recorded here so the exercise is accounted for.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd edition), Example 10.7, §10.3, printed page 276 (PDF page 285) — item `awodey:10.3:example7`.

Awodey derives the same monad from the free ⊣ forgetful adjunction between sets and monoids: `T(X)` is the set of finite strings over `X`, the unit is the one-element string and the multiplication is concatenation of a string of strings. A `T`-algebra is a map compatible with flattening; every monoid yields one by taking products, the monoid structure is recovered from the structure map as `α(empty)` and `x · y = α(x,y)`, and every `T`-algebra arises from a unique monoid — so the Eilenberg–Moore category of this monad *is* the category of monoids.

In-tree state: the list monad's operations exist but only in the deliberately law-free FP layer (`Theory/Coq/List.v:113` `list_Monad`, whose `Monad` class carries no laws — `Theory/Coq/Monad/Proofs.v` proves `IsMonad` only for `Identity`, `arrow` and `Compose`), and a category of internal monoids with a faithful forgetful functor exists (`Theory/Algebra/Monoid/Hom.v:83` `Mon`, `:93` `Mon_Forget`, `:101` `Mon_Forget_Faithful`) but has no left adjoint. The nearest proved theorem, `Theory/Multicategory/Algebra.v:686` `Comm_algebra_CMon`, is about algebras for the terminal *operad* and *commutative* monoids — a different statement.

- [ ] (from Awodey §10.3) the correspondence packaged as an equivalence of categories between the Eilenberg–Moore category of the monad and the category of monoids, commuting with the two forgetful functors to sets.

The exercise asks for one direction of the correspondence explicitly: given an algebra for the monad induced by the free ⊣ forgetful adjunction between sets and monoids, exhibit the multiplication and the unit element it determines on the carrier, and check that the monoid laws follow from the algebra unit and associativity laws. ### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd edition), §10.3, unnumbered construction, printed page 277 (PDF page 286) — item `awodey:10.3:construction-comparison-functor`.

Awodey states the same obligation: from an arbitrary adjunction with induced monad `T`, there is a comparison functor into the Eilenberg–Moore category satisfying `U^T ∘ Φ ≅ U` and `Φ ∘ F = F^T`, and `Φ` is **unique** with that property — which is what exhibits the Eilenberg–Moore category as terminal among the categories inducing `T`.

Useful in-tree state for whoever takes this issue: the existence half and *both* commutations are already proved — `Monad/Comparison.v:186` `EM_Comparison`, `:198` `EM_Comparison_Forget`, `:260` `EM_Comparison_Free` (with the algebra on `U c` given by `fmap[U] (counit c)` at `:151`). The work that remains for Awodey's clause is exactly the uniqueness statement this issue names: nothing of the form `∀ K, EM_Forget ◯ K ≈ U → K ◯ F ≈ EM_Free → K ≈ EM_Comparison` exists, and searches for uniqueness lemmas across `Monad/` and `Comonad/` turn up only `lift_factor_unique`, `em_reflect_desc_unique`, `created_algebra_unique` and `EM_extend_unique`, none of them about the comparison functor.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd edition), §10.3, unnumbered remark, printed page 277 (PDF page 286) — item `awodey:10.3:remark-kleisli-nonuniqueness`.

Awodey makes the same point this issue formalises: every monad arises from an adjunction, but the inducing triple is **not** unique — besides the Eilenberg–Moore category there is the Kleisli category, generally different, also carrying an adjoint pair that induces the same monad.

In-tree state: the positive content is complete on both sides — `Monad/Eilenberg/Moore/Adjunction.v:183` `EM_Adjunction` with `:219` `EM_Monad_agrees`, and `Monad/Kleisli/Adjunction.v:125` `Kleisli_Adjunction` with `:146` `Kleisli_join_agrees` and `:157` `Kleisli_Monad_agrees`. What is missing is precisely the *separating* and *extremal* content this issue is about: there is no comparison functor from the Kleisli category into the Eilenberg–Moore category (a search for either name inside the other returns nothing; the Kleisli-side comparison is #475), no instance where the two are shown inequivalent, and no initial/terminal characterisation of the two resolutions.

- [ ] (from Awodey §10.3) **library defect to fix while here:** `Monad/Eilenberg/Moore/Adjunction.v:48-50` and `Monad/Eilenberg/Moore.v:34-35` assert in their header essays that the Kleisli resolution is initial and that "its comparison into `C^T`" exists; neither is backed by any in-tree artifact. Either prove them here or soften those lines to forward references.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd edition), §10.3, unnumbered example, printed page 278 (PDF page 287) — item `awodey:10.3:example-pos-not-monadic`.

Awodey runs the identical argument with posets in place of spaces: the underlying-set functor from posets to sets is a right adjoint (its left adjoint is the discrete-poset functor), the unit at any set is the identity, so the induced monad is the identity monad, whose Eilenberg–Moore category is the base itself — hence the comparison functor is not an equivalence and the functor is not monadic. The reusable half of the argument is already in-tree as `Monad/Monadicity/Examples.v:145` `identity_monadic`, which proves that the Eilenberg–Moore category of the identity monad is equivalent to the base.

- [ ] (from Awodey §10.3) the poset instance: the discrete-poset functor as left adjoint to the underlying-set functor on `Pos`, the induced monad computed to be the identity, and the resulting failure of monadicity (needs the category of posets from #641).

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd edition), §10.5, unnumbered remark, printed page 283 (PDF page 292) — item `awodey:10.5:remark-nat-initial-algebra`.

Same obligation: the usual recursion property of the natural numbers — zero together with successor, i.e. the single arrow out of `1 + N` — says *precisely* that the naturals with zero and successor form the initial algebra of the endofunctor `X ↦ 1 + X`; equivalently, for every set with a distinguished point and an endomap there is a unique map from the naturals commuting with both.

In-tree state, which makes this cheap: the endofunctor is already built and proved functorial as `Theory/Adamek/Corollaries.v:87` `NatF X := option X`, and the structurally identical result one parameter up is fully proved at `Instance/Coq/Lists.v:111` `list_initial` (for `1 + A × X`). What is absent is any term exhibiting the naturals as an algebra at all, and any `@Initial (FAlg NatF)`.

- [ ] (from Awodey §10.5) the in-tree instantiation: `@Initial (FAlg NatF)` proved for the naturals with zero and successor, **and** the self-disclaimer at `Theory/Adamek/Corollaries.v:76-80` ("the initial-algebra theorem … is not stated in the tree") retired or updated to point at the proof.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd edition), Exercise 10.6.1(a)–(b), printed page 290 (PDF page 299) — item `awodey:10:ex1` (parts (a) and (b); part (c) is recorded on #252).

Awodey frames the natural numbers object as the initial model of the equational theory with one constant symbol, one unary function symbol and no axioms, in any category with a terminal object, and asks for two things: that the naturals with zero and successor form such an object in sets, and that any natural numbers object is *uniquely* isomorphic to it as a model of that theory.

In-tree state: there is no natural-numbers-object notion at all, no initial-model notion for an equational theory (`Theory/Lawvere/Model.v` defines models but proves nothing about an initial one), and no instantiated "initial objects are unique up to a unique isomorphism" lemma — `Structure/Initial.v` offers only `zero_unique` (uniqueness of the mediator, `:112`), and the general representability result `Structure/UniversalProperty.v:175` is never instantiated at initial or terminal objects.

- [ ] (from Awodey §10.6 Ex 1) the naturals with zero and successor exhibited as a natural numbers object in sets.
- [ ] (from Awodey §10.6 Ex 1) any natural numbers object proved uniquely isomorphic to it *as a model* of the one-constant, one-unary-operation theory — i.e. the isomorphism commutes with zero and successor and is the unique such map.

### Also covered by

Awodey, *Category Theory* (2nd edition), Exercise 10.6.1(c), printed page 290 (PDF page 299) — item `awodey:10:ex1` (part (c) only; parts (a) and (b) are recorded on #637).

Part (c) asks for exactly this issue's statement in its uniqueness form: the naturals with zero and successor are characterised **up to isomorphism** as the initial algebra for the endofunctor `X ↦ X + 1`.

- [ ] (from Awodey §10.6 Ex 1c) the characterisation up to isomorphism, not merely the existence of the initial algebra: any initial algebra for `X ↦ X + 1` is isomorphic to the naturals with zero and successor, by an isomorphism of algebras.
